{{Quote|You'll need the orbital drift charts to clear the Peragus asteroid field, unless you want to have the shortest flight out of Peragus ever recorded.|Atton Rand|<ref name="TSL">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords]]''</ref>}}
[[File:PeragusAsteroidField.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Drift charts for the Peragus asteroid field enabled the Jedi Exile's ''Ebon Hawk'' to leave it.]]
'''Asteroid orbital drift charts'''<ref name="TSL" /> were [[Computer/Legends|computer]]-based simulations of the movement of various bodies that occupied an [[Asteroid field/Legends|asteroid field]].<ref name="CSWE">{{CSWECite|I|208|drift chart}}</ref> Stored in a [[Navigation computer/Legends|navigation computer]], orbital drift charts formed a part of a ship's astrogation capabilities, allowing it to navigate an asteroid field safely.<ref name="TSL" />

The [[Peragus Mining Facility]]'s command [[Computer/Legends|console]] stored asteroid drift charts that were constantly updated, allowing the console to send out transmissions to incoming crafts to prevent them from being crushed into [[Realspace/Legends|space]] dust. Prior to the transmission of orbital drift charts, the Peragus console automatically hailed incoming ships, usually [[Freighter/Legends|freighters]], to warn them to maintain distance as well as to send them docking instructions<ref name="TSL" />

When the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic]] [[Warship/Legends|warship]] [[Harbinger (Hammerhead-class)|''Harbinger'']] arrived at the Peragus Mining Facility, where the [[Meetra Surik|Jedi Exile]] and her freighter, the ''[[Ebon Hawk]]'', was trapped in, the exile and her companions, [[Atton Rand]] and [[Kreia]], boarded the ''Harbinger'' and stole the drift charts to the [[Peragus asteroid field]] stored in its navicomputer, bringing them to the ''Ebon Hawk'' and making their escape.<ref name="TSL" />
